newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard earnings up, but disappoint Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard earnings up, but disappoint Wall St.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co., citing sluggish order and revenue growth, on Thursday reported an 8 percent rise in net earnings for its fiscal second quarter but fell short of Wall Street expectations.
The company said a tough comparison with a strong quarter last year, the effect of a stronger dollar and slowing in some markets constrained growth rates.

Industry analysts also cited weaker-than-expected growth in Hewlett-Packard's inkjet printer business and a decline in orders and revenue for its LaserJet printers. Hewlett-Packard said overall U.S. orders fell 2 percent during the quarter, while orders outside the United States rose by 7 percent.

Net earnings for the quarter were $784 million, or 75 cents a share, compared with $723 million, or 69 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Those results were restated to reflect a two-for-one stock split completed in July 1996.
Hewlett-Packard's results came in below industry analysts' estimates of 80 cents a share, according to First Call, which monitors Wall Street earnings projections.

Analysts said the company outlined a myriad of smaller issues in its conference call, including weakness in high end server computers to be addressed by launch of a powerful new product next week and concerns about maturing of its printer business.
"It resembles a big ship that is a little bit off course," said JP Morgan analyst Daniel Kunstler. "They're a little bit mispositioned vis-a-vis the markets they intend to serve."
Revenue for the quarter ended April 30 was $10.3 billion, up 5 percent from $9.9 billion in last year's second quarter.

Revenues in the third quarter could be flat to weaker, analysts said, but they are still expected to be well above levels a year ago when the company issued a profit warning which rattled the entire high-flying technology sector.

The results were released after the close of stock trading. Hewlett-Packard shares were halted at the close, with the last trade up $2.25 at $58.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, just shy of the day's high of $59 and the stock's all-time trading high of $60.

Analysts said the share price had run up in hopes Hewlett-Packard would provide a positive result and could fall $5 or more Friday, but there was little in the report and subsequent conference call that should cause a broader selloff in the high tech sector.
"It might take them a while to get back to $59," one said.
Hewlett-Packard Chairman Lewis Platt said the company managed to generate good profit margins despite the slowing order growth.
"Our cost-of-sales result was excellent, and we continued to make progress in managing our operating assets and in generating cash," Platt said in a statement.
"We're disappointed, however, with order and revenue growth," he said. "A tough comparison with last year, as well as currency effects and slowing in some markets, affected our growth rates."
Executives told analysts in a conference call that new product intrductions should also help it in the second half.
Revenue in the United States was $4.4 billion, an increase of 1 percent from the year-ago quarter, while revenue from outside the United States rose 7 percent to $5.9 billion.

Orders for the quarter totalled $10.4 billion, a 3 percent rise from a year ago, when orders had jumped 24 percent from the year-earlier period. Without the effects of currency-exchange rates, the company's order growth this quarter would have been about 3 percentage points higher, Hewlett-Packard said.
In the United States, orders declined 2 percent to $4.6 billion, while orders from outside the United States rose 7 percent to $5.8 billion.
David Wu, an analyst at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp., noted that the most marked weakness in orders was in the United States, and said "you can't blame the dollar for that."
"The quarter is bad but it was not disastrous," Wu added. "If you're a contrarian this is a good time to buy."
